title: Implementation Guidelines for E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2016
citation: CPCB, HWM Division. Guidelines under E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2016 (G.S.R. 338(E), 23 March 2016, effective 1 October 2016)
currency: SUPERSEDED. The 2016 rules were replaced by the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 (G.S.R. 801(E), in force 1 April 2023), which the library now holds as ewaste_rules_2022.

scope.applies_to: Producers, consumers, bulk consumers, collection centres, dismantlers and recyclers of electrical and electronic equipment in Schedule I: IT and telecom equipment, and consumer electricals and electronics including fluorescent and other mercury-containing lamps.

key_points.text: Consumers should channelise e-waste through collection centres or dealers of authorised producers, dismantlers or recyclers, or the producer's take-back service, and should not throw e-waste in municipal bins.
End-of-life fluorescent and other mercury-containing lamps are not to go in the municipal bin; hand them, properly packed and upright, to the producer take-back or an authorised collection centre.
Bulk consumers hand e-waste only to producer take-back or authorised dismantlers or recyclers, and keep special bins for intact end-of-life lamps.
EPR collection targets for producers rise from 30% of estimated generation in the first two years to 70% from the seventh year.

routing_implications.summary: E-waste goes through producer take-back and authorised collection centres, not municipal routes. Under SWM Rules 2026 r. 9(7)(ii), a registered MRF may act as a deposition centre for e-waste for onward channelisation.
routing_implications.overlap_with_swm: SWM Rules 2026 r. 3(1)(zx) lists CFLs, bulbs and tube lights as household special care waste collected via deposition centres (r. 39(48)). Treat lamps at deposition centres or MRFs as e-waste to be handed to the producer channel.
